summary: St. Lawrence County tower: wood tower 1911, 35-foot steel tower 1917, closed 1970 or 1971, removed early 1980s; foundations remain on a trail open on private land.

facts.design: 35-foot Aermotor LS40 steel tower (1917), replacing a wooden log-framed pyramid tower (1911)
facts.status_note: Tower and cabin removed in the early 1980s; their foundations remain on the summit.

access.note: Trail network on private land, open to the public; parking is near Catamount Lodge with a trail map in a box by the fence.

visit.trail_note: 2.5-mile out-and-back from the parking area south of the lodge, about 420 feet of climbing; there is no tower to climb.

facts.agency: New York State Conservation Department, precursor to the DEC

events.note: A wooden log-framed pyramid tower with no cab was built on the summit
The wood tower was replaced with a 35-foot steel Aermotor LS40 tower
A new observer's cabin was built; the newsletter author could find no photos of it
A fire near Mud Lake threatened wide destruction; a phone on a service truck linked the ranger to the observer in the tower; more than 200 fighters worked the blaze
William McDonald returned to the tower as a fire spotter
Observer Miles McCarthy spotted a blaze south of South Colton; the fire, of unknown origin, started when a hunting camp burned
Closed at the end of the 1971 fire lookout season; a 2018 blog says 1970
New York Telephone Company built a relay station with an 80-foot antenna on the summit

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Wikipedia and the Adirondack Explorer say the tower closed at the end of the 1971 fire season; a 2018 blog says the end of the 1970 season. The story gives both.

Wikipedia says the tower stood on private land; the Explorer says the trail network is on private property but open to the public. The story reports public access on private land, as the Explorer describes it.

notes_for_editor: Build dates (1911 wood, 1917 steel) and the 1925 cabin are well supported. Closing year conflicts (1970 vs 1971). The Adirondack Explorer article's publication date does not appear in the text I read, so the today description is undated; it says the tower and cabin were removed by the early 1980s. The tower access note is taken from the Explorer, which says the trail network is on private property but open to the public. No photos were added.
